title: Quantization performance & kernel benchmark: INT8 / FP8 / GPTQ / AWQ
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the design, methodology, and preliminary results from our quantization performance vs. quality benchmark sweep. We compared INT8 (symmetric/asymmetric), FP8 (E4M3), GPTQ (4-bit/8-bit variants) and AWQ-style weight quantization across multiple kernel implementations to understand runtime throughput/latency, memory usage, and end-task quality impact on representative LLMs. The goal is to drive kernel selection and runtime fallback policy decisions for Redwood serving profiles.

Summary / quick takeaways:
- INT8 kernels (optimized GEMM + custom dequant path) give the best throughput lift on A100 when sequence length <= 512 and batch size >= 4, but can show non-trivial generation quality regressions on some instruction-following prompts (higher token error rate vs FP16 baseline).
- AWQ/GPTQ 4-bit variants provide the strongest model-size reduction and memory bandwidth savings; throughput improvements depend heavily on the kernel packing strategy and how we implement kv-cache dequant.
- FP8 (E4M3) offers a middle ground: modest throughput gains versus FP16 and generally minimal quality degradation on open-vocabulary tasks; kernel maturity (hw support + optimized matmul) is lower and varies by hardware (H100 shows stronger gains than A100).
- Kernel choice matters more than quant format: naive cuBLAS int8 paths are often slower than a well-tuned fused-int8 kernel that prunes dequantization and reorder costs.
- Profiling hotspots: GEMM (matmul), weight dequant, memory-bound kv-cache operations, and attention softmax for long sequences.

Benchmarks & setup:
- Models: Llama-2-13B (decoder-only), mix-quant runs with Llama-2-7B as a secondary check.
- HW: NVIDIA A100 (40GB & 80GB nodes), H100 (80GB) and T4 for smaller tests.
- OS / drivers: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1 (H100 optimized), cuBLAS 12.x, Triton runtime (for some custom kernels), and our in-house fused-kernel lib v0.9.
- Framework / runtime: Redwood serving-runtime commit sha: 0a1b2c3 (linked PR above). Tests run in dedicated-mode (no noisy neighbors).
- Sequence lengths: 32, 128, 512, 1024. Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8. Sampling: greedy + top-k for latency-sensitive checks.
- Metrics collected: tokens/sec (throughput), p50/p95 generation latency, peak GPU memory, CPU overhead (dequant + scheduling), and quality metrics (perplexity on Wikitext-103, instruction-following score on a 120 prompt eval set, token error rate vs FP16).

Kernel variants tested:
- cuBLAS-based matmul + host-side dequant (baseline naive INT8 on cuBLAS)
- Fused INT8 kernels (our custom fused-dequant+matmul)
- Triton microkernels (TP-wise matmul with int8 packing)
- FP8 native kernels (where supported) + fallback path to FP16 matmul for unsupported ops
- GPTQ-style kernel pack (4-bit) + fast unpack + fused accumulation
- AWQ-style per-block quant + specialized dequant kernel for KV cache

Representative results (Llama-2-13B, A100-80GB, seq=128, batch=4):
- FP16 baseline: 110 tokens/sec, p50=220ms, peak GPU mem=52GB, perplexity=8.2 (Wikitext)
- INT8 naive (cuBLAS+host dequant): 95 tokens/sec, p50=260ms, peak GPU mem=36GB, perplexity=10.6
- INT8 fused kernel: 145 tokens/sec, p50=175ms, peak GPU mem=36GB, perplexity=10.3
- FP8 (E4M3, hw-accelerated on H100): 130 tokens/sec (A100: 118 tokens/sec), p50=185ms, peak GPU mem=34GB, perplexity=8.9
- GPTQ 4-bit (packed, fused-dequant): 210 tokens/sec, p50=110ms, peak GPU mem=28GB, perplexity=12.8
- AWQ 4-bit (block-quant + specialized kv dequant): 200 tokens/sec, p50=115ms, peak GPU mem=29GB, perplexity=11.9
Notes: numbers above are median from 5 runs. GPTQ/AWQ 4-bit runs achieved the biggest memory reductions and throughput gains but at higher perplexity and noticeable divergence on instruction-following (instruction score drop ~15-25% relative to FP16).

Profiling observations (flamegraphs + nvprof):
- For INT8 naive path, 35% of wall-time is spent in host-side dequant and data reorder (PCIe pinned host copies are a contention point).
- Fused-int8 kernel reduces host-side work to <5% and shifts bottleneck to GEMM compute (good). Memory-bound kernels still limited by L2 bandwidth for KV cache reads.
- GPTQ/AWQ paths: packing/unpacking and bit-manipulation kernels dominate for small sequences; for larger sequences the matmul stage dominates but benefits from smaller working set fitting L2/L1.
- FP8 on H100: hardware support reduces compute cycles, but our kernel implementation still has some scalar conversion overheads (half-vector conversions) that we can optimize.

Quality analysis:
- Perplexity vs FP16 baseline: FP8 ~ +0.7-1.2, INT8 ~ +2.0-2.4, GPTQ/AWQ 4-bit ~ +4.0-6.5 (varies by prompt mix).
- Instruction-following eval: FP8 <5% drop, INT8 ~10-15% drop, GPTQ/AWQ ~15-30% drop depending on the prompt distribution and whether we quantized attention/query/key/ffn differently.
- Failure modes: hallucinations on longer multi-turn prompts, token repetition loops, and token-level coherence failures most common on 4-bit runs.

Recommendations (short-term):
1) Default-serving profile: offer FP8 (E4M3) where hardware supports it (H100 preferred), falling back to fused-INT8 on A100 for seq length <=512 and batch>=4. This balances throughput/quality for most production workloads.
2) Expose quality-preserving toggle: "aggressive-quant" for customers who prioritize cost/throughput (GPTQ/AWQ 4-bit) with explicit warning and optional A/B testing flags.
3) Kernel work: invest in fused dequant+matmul kernels (Triton + CUDA) and optimize AWQ/GPTQ pack/unpack to run on-GPU with minimal CPU involvement.
4) KV cache path: implement blockwise dequant in the KV read path to avoid a full-token-level dequant per step (reduces p50 for single-token generations).
5) Telemetry: add quant-mode quality hooks in Optimize to track instruction-eval regressions per model/commit.

Open action items / next experiments:
- Re-run the sweep on H100 with mixed FP8+GPTQ experiments where FFN layers use higher precision (2-1 mixed quantization).
- Microbenchmark attention softmax and rotary embedding kernels under quantized weight inputs to measure numerical stability.
- Implement a Triton-based AWQ pack/unpack and measure host-CPU overhead reduction.
- Add customer-facing docs explaining quality tradeoffs + sample prompts for calibration.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc: numbers are from internal runs and should be reproduced from the linked PR + run artifacts. Expect variance across different PRs/driver versions.
- See linked artifacts for run ids and the PR that landed the fused-int8 kernels.

Appendix: brief methodology checklist used for each run:
- cold start node, pinned to single job, disable other services
- run 3 warmup sequences then 5 measured runs; discard first run
- ensure deterministic prompt set and random seeds for sampling tests
- collect nvprof + Triton logs + GPU utilization and CPU profiles

End of doc.
